item.title: Re: A question
item.content:encoded: Safe containment usually entails "just sticking it in a box or locker without having to worry about it." This one needs a gelatin cube (that needs to be monitored for degradation), surgically deafened D-Class, high grade ear protections, multiple pairs of tongs to carry it so it doesn't ring. I know this is all opinions on fiction, but I'm in the camp that this certainly isn't Safe.

item.title: A question
item.content:encoded:
Howdy!
I love the SCP that you wrote, real creepy. I have a question though. Since the actual object can be reliably contained, would it not have a safe classification? Yes I understand that if you ring it, bad stuff happens, but otherwise if left alone, nothing else occurs. If it is Euclid because of SCP-513-1, then that would work, but I just feel that the bell itself can be easily contained. Let me know what you think. Adios!

item.title: Re: How to permanently contain SCP-513

item.title: Re: How to permanently contain SCP-513
item.content:encoded: Gelatin's actually the best way to immobilize it totally. As for why they don't destroy it, the reason is the same as for any other object: if containment is working, there's no reason to destroy it. Destroying things frequently only makes things worse. For all they know, that bell is all that binds the entity from running free.

item.title: How to permanently contain SCP-513
item.content:encoded:
1. Remove it from its gelatin container and place it on the floor
2. Smash it with a sledgehammer.
3. One less SCP object to worry about.

But seriously though what is the point of keeping this thing around if they could easily just as well destroy it? Like, if it's a dangerous object and can possibly cause death, WHY DO YOU BOTHER KEEPING IT AROUND!? Not to mention, they are putting it in a container that can easily be broken open, exposing the damn thing. ALSO, the container will just deteriorate over time, so why not just duct tape it so it can't make noise, then just toss it into a metal container and lock it up? I just don't see the point in having it in a container that can be destroyed easily, and I'm not gonna question why they don't just tear it apart.

item.title: Actually...
item.content:encoded:
In response to number 3, it doesn't appear (to me anyway) that the object itself makes you crazy.
Instead it seems like precisely the kind of reaction someone would sooner or later have to the stated effects.
It doesn't make you magically crazy to death because "you cannot grasp the true form" or something like that, it stalks, hunts and prevents you from sleeping until you go crazy to the point that you really don't see an alternative to suicide.
How would you react to that? (Please don't take it as a verbal attack, I really wonder how else anyone could possibly react to it. )
